answer: I would like to talk about the person whose food I would choose over any restaurant's. The best cook I know is my mother, whose food has a reputation among everyone who has ever tasted it. She cooks almost every meal for our family, and her specialities are traditional Bengali dishes like hilsa in mustard sauce, beef curry and, at Eid, a rich biryani that relatives talk about for weeks. She never followed formal recipes; instead she learned from her own mother as a girl and refined everything through years of practice. What makes her cooking special is her [[intuitive]] sense of flavour; she seems to know exactly how much of each spice to add without measuring. Her traditional dishes are genuinely [[exquisite]], and guests often ask for the recipes, which she happily shares. I think part of what makes her food so good is the care she puts into it; cooking for her is an act of love, not a chore. Whenever the family gathers, her kitchen becomes [[the beating heart]] of the house. As for how I feel about her cooking, it is simply the taste of home to me, and even a plain bowl of dal tastes better when she makes it. Honestly, no restaurant has ever quite matched the comfort of a meal she has prepared. I only wish I had paid closer attention over the years, because her skill feels almost [[irreplaceable]], and if I do study abroad one day, it is the thing I will miss most.

followUps.answer: Only a few basic dishes, like rice, dal and an omelette. I really need to learn more before I study abroad, so I have started asking my mother to teach me, though I am a rather [[clumsy]] pupil.

followUps.q: Do you prefer home-cooked food or eating out?
followUps.answer: Home-cooked food, without a doubt. Eating out is enjoyable occasionally, but restaurant food is often too oily for me, and nothing beats sitting down to dinner with my family.
